app.name: Proloquo
app.description: An intuitive Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) app designed for all ages. Features a large vocabulary, word prediction, and a unique Thinking Space mode for visual communication.

verdict.one_liner: A thoughtfully designed AAC app with strong privacy protections, explicit no-ads commitments, and excellent safeguards for children — though some data goes to US servers and optional health information can be collected.
verdict.summary: Proloquo is an augmentative communication app designed for people who need help speaking. Its privacy policy is unusually clear and respectful: the company explicitly promises never to sell your data or use it for ads, your actual communication messages never leave your device, and there are strong protections for children including parent-controlled data sharing. However, some data is stored on US servers, optional health diagnosis information can be collected, and policy changes are accepted passively if you keep using the app.
verdict.recommendation_reason: The app demonstrates strong privacy ethics with clear no-ads and no-selling commitments, local-only message processing, and robust child protections. The remaining concerns (US data storage, optional health data, passive policy acceptance) are relatively minor for an app of this type.

red.title: Some data stored on US servers
red.plain_english: Your information is stored on computers in both Europe and the United States. The United States has weaker privacy laws than Europe, which means your data may not be protected as strongly.

red.title: Optional medical diagnosis collected
red.plain_english: When setting up a user profile, you can optionally enter a medical diagnosis. While this helps with support, it means sensitive health information is stored on their servers.

red.title: Policy changes accepted automatically
red.plain_english: If they update the privacy rules, you will get a notification. But if you keep using the app after that, it counts as agreeing to the new rules — you don't have to click 'I agree'.

green.title: No ads and data is never sold
green.plain_english: The company explicitly promises they will never sell your personal data, and they will never use it for advertising or marketing purposes.

green.title: Your messages stay on your device
green.plain_english: The sentences and messages you create to communicate are processed entirely on your phone or tablet. They are never sent to AssistiveWare or anyone else.

green.title: Strong protections for children
green.plain_english: The app follows strict child privacy laws like COPPA and GDPR. Parents or guardians control what data is collected and who can see it.

green.title: Extra data sharing requires your consent
green.plain_english: If they want to collect more than basic anonymous usage stats, they ask for your explicit permission first. You can say no without breaking the app.

categories.label: Camera & Microphone
categories.plain_english: The app lets you upload photos for personalizing communication symbols. This is entirely optional and only happens when you choose to do it.
categories.detail: Users can upload photos for personalization (user-specific words, symbols). This is on-demand, optional, and user-initiated. There is no mention of background camera or microphone access, and uploaded content is not shared with third parties.
categories.policy_excerpt: their personalization (user specific words, uploaded photos)

categories.label: Location & GPS
categories.plain_english: The app does not track your location.
categories.detail: No location or GPS data collection is mentioned anywhere in the privacy policy.

categories.label: Contacts & Phonebook
categories.plain_english: The app does not access your phone's contacts list.
categories.detail: AAC Team members are invited via a link sent by the admin, not through contacts or phonebook access. There is no mention of contacts or phonebook data collection.

categories.label: Storage & File Access
categories.plain_english: You can save backups of your vocabulary and settings to your own computer or cloud services like iCloud, Dropbox, or Google Drive. AssistiveWare cannot access these backups.
categories.detail: The app allows AAC Team admins to back up device data to local storage or third-party cloud services. AssistiveWare explicitly states they have no access to these backups and cannot guarantee protection of data stored there.
categories.policy_excerpt: The applications allow the AAC Team admin to store a backup of the device data ... on a local computer or in third party cloud storage, such as iCloud, Dropbox or Google Drive. AssistiveWare has no access to these back up storages.
concerns: Third-party cloud backup security outside AssistiveWare control

categories.label: Data Sharing with 3rd Parties
categories.plain_english: Your data is only shared with people on your AAC Team, service providers who help run the app, and legal authorities if required by law. It is never sold.
categories.detail: AssistiveWare explicitly commits to never selling personal data or using it for advertising, profiling, or marketing. Data is shared only with authorized AAC Team members, external service providers under data processing agreements, and government authorities when legally required.
categories.policy_excerpt: We will never sell your personal data to third parties, nor will we use or share your personal data for third party advertising, -profiling or -marketing purposes.
concerns: Data processed by external service providers
Data may be disclosed to authorities under legal obligation

categories.label: Account & Identity Data
categories.plain_english: You need to provide your name, email, and country to create an account. For the person using the app to communicate, only a first name is required.
categories.detail: Account registration requires name, email address, and country of residence. For the AAC User, first name is mandatory; birth year and diagnosis are optional. Organization users may provide additional details. This data is used for licensing and support, not for advertising.
categories.policy_excerpt: we collect and process the personal data you provide, such as your name, email address, country of residence

categories.label: Behavioural & Ad Tracking
categories.plain_english: The app does not show ads and does not track your behavior for advertising purposes.
categories.detail: AssistiveWare explicitly states they do not use or share personal data for third-party advertising, profiling, or marketing. Anonymous usage data is collected for product improvement and research only.
categories.policy_excerpt: We will never sell your personal data to third parties, nor will we use or share your personal data for third party advertising, -profiling or -marketing purposes.

categories.label: Children's Data Handling
categories.plain_english: The app is designed with strong protections for children, including parent controls and compliance with child privacy laws.
categories.detail: AssistiveWare recognizes the importance of protecting minors. The app minimizes data collection from children, lets parents/guardians control data sharing through the AAC Team admin role, and complies with COPPA and GDPR. For school use, AssistiveWare acts only as a data processor.
categories.policy_excerpt: We limit the collection and processing of personal data of minors as much as possible... We let the AAC Team admin (e.g. a parent) control the collection and use of the personal data of the minor

categories.label: Network & Internet Activity
categories.plain_english: The app needs an internet connection to sync your vocabulary and settings between devices used by your AAC Team.
categories.detail: The app requires internet connectivity to sync AAC User vocabulary, settings, and personalization across AAC Team devices. Standard network logging (IP addresses, etc.) occurs for security and service provision.
concerns: Internet required for core syncing functionality

categories.label: Device Info & Fingerprinting
categories.plain_english: The app collects anonymous information about your device, like the device type and app version, to help improve the product.
categories.detail: Anonymous device information (device type, app version, settings) is collected for product improvement and research. This data is not linked to the person using the app and cannot be used to identify them.
categories.policy_excerpt: We collect data on the application usage, including, but not limited to, the application version, device information, application settings and application usage statistics. The data is not linked to the person using the product, nor can it be used to disclose the identity of the user.

categories.label: Health & Biometric Data
categories.plain_english: You can optionally enter a medical diagnosis when setting up a user profile. This sensitive information is stored on their servers but is not sold or shared.
categories.detail: The AAC User's diagnosis is an optional field collected to improve products and provide appropriate support. While sensitive health data, it is not shared with third parties or used for advertising. Birth year is also optional.
categories.policy_excerpt: The AAC User's birth year and diagnose are non-mandatory fields. The information about age and/or diagnose is used to improve our products and to have an appropriate conversation with the AAC Team in connection with support request.
concerns: Optional health diagnosis stored on servers

categories.label: Financial & Payment Data
categories.plain_english: Payments are handled entirely through Apple's App Store. AssistiveWare never sees your credit card or payment details.
categories.detail: The app uses Apple's in-app subscription system. AssistiveWare does not directly process or store payment card information.

categories.label: Data Deletion & User Rights
categories.plain_english: You can request to see, change, or delete your data. However, they keep AAC User data for 18 months after your subscription ends unless you specifically ask them to delete it sooner.
categories.detail: Users have rights to access, amend, delete, transfer, restrict, and object to data processing. Complaints can be filed with data protection authorities. AAC User data is retained for 18 months after license expiration unless deletion is requested. Account deletion removes AAC Team member data.
categories.policy_excerpt: You have the right to request access to or the amendment, deletion or data transfer of your personal data... We retain personal data of the AAC User for a period of eighteen (18) months after expiration of a license.

categories.label: Policy Change Notification
categories.plain_english: If they make important changes to the privacy rules, they will tell you. But if you keep using the app afterwards, that counts as accepting the new rules.
categories.detail: Material changes to privacy processing trigger a notification. However, continued use of the app after changes constitutes acceptance. Users are advised to review the policy periodically.
categories.policy_excerpt: If we make material changes to how we process your personal data, we will send you a notification thereof. Your continued use of the application(s) after changes to the privacy statement will deemed to be your acceptance of such changes.
